claims.text: A machine-learning framework can optimize thermo-mechanical processing parameters for conventional metallic materials.
Machine-learning-optimized processing can systematically produce a dual-phase microstructure.
The resulting dual-phase microstructure simultaneously improves strength and ductility relative to homogeneous processing.
The initial material has a homogeneous microstructure produced by standard thermo-mechanical processing.
The machine-learning model integrates rolling reduction, annealing temperature and time, aging steps, and microstructural evolution.
The optimized route produces a dual-phase or inverted microstructure.
The targeted microstructure contains discrete nanoscale precipitates dispersed in a continuous ductile matrix.
The machine-learning model assimilates historical experimental data to predict an optimal combination of thermo-mechanical processing parameters.
The predicted processing parameters create a balanced distribution of strengthening precipitates and ductile matrix.
Balancing strengthening precipitates with a ductile matrix overcomes the strength-ductility trade-off.
Machine-learning-optimized processing yields higher yield strength than conventional processing.
Machine-learning-optimized processing yields higher tensile strength than conventional processing.
Machine-learning-optimized processing maintains or improves ductility relative to conventional processing.
Conventional grain refinement and precipitation hardening typically enhance strength at the cost of ductility.
The proposed approach is applicable to metallic systems under ambient conditions using scalable thermo-mechanical techniques.
